title: Shohei Ohtani Set to Pitch Next Season, Uncertain About Off‑Season Surgery Plans – MLB Trade Rumors
body:
Shohei Ohtan​i’s future on the mound remains uncertain as the Los Angeles Angels head into the offseason, with the Japanese phenom hinting that he may return to pitching duties next year while leaving the question of any corrective surgery wide open. The two‑way star’s performance in the final stretch of the 2024 campaign — a slump at the plate and a lingering elbow issue that kept him off the rotation after mid‑July — has sparked a flurry of speculation about his health and how the Angels will manage his rare skill set moving forward.

In the postseason, Ohtani’s bat was far from his usual prodigious output, posting a .160/.284/.253 line over 88 plate appearances and a wRC+ of just 58, well below his career norm. The decline was most evident after the All‑Star break, when his swing appeared tentative and his power numbers evaporated. Meanwhile, his pitching résumé for the year ended abruptly in early July, when a lingering elbow discomfort forced him onto the injured list. Though he has not taken the mound since, Ohtani has not ruled out pitching again, saying he intends to “see what the body allows” and that “it’s hard to tell” whether any surgical intervention will be necessary.

The dual‑role demands placed on Ohtani are unprecedented in modern baseball, and his recent health concerns underscore the delicate balance the Angels must strike. Medical staff have reportedly been monitoring his elbow with regular imaging, and while no definitive diagnosis has been disclosed, the team appears cautious about committing to an invasive procedure that could sideline him for an extended period. Ohtani’s own comments suggest a preference for a conservative approach, emphasizing conditioning and incremental workloads over immediate surgery. This stance aligns with the Angels’ broader strategy of preserving his long‑term value, both as a power hitter and a frontline starter.

Analysts are divided on how the Angels should allocate Ohtani’s talents next season. Some argue that focusing on his pitching could extend his career and provide the club with a rare ace who can also contribute offensively, especially given the scarcity of elite two‑way players. Others contend that his offensive ceiling remains unparalleled and that limiting his pitching duties would reduce injury risk while maximizing his impact at the plate. The team’s front office is reportedly weighing both options, with potential scenarios ranging from a full‑time rotation role, a limited‑innings approach, or a return to primarily hitting with occasional spot starts.

The implications extend beyond Los Angeles. Ohtani’s health and role have become a touchstone for discussions about player utilization across the league, influencing how clubs evaluate the viability of two‑way athletes. If Ohtani successfully returns to pitching without sacrificing his batting prowess, it could inspire a new wave of talent development focused on versatility. Conversely, a setback could reinforce the conventional wisdom that specialization remains the safest path for elite performance.

As the offseason progresses, the Angels are expected to provide more concrete updates on Ohtani’s medical status and his projected workload for 2025. Fans and analysts alike will be watching for any indication of surgery, rehabilitation timelines, or adjustments to his training regimen. Regardless of the outcome, Ohtani’s willingness to confront uncertainty and his commitment to contributing in multiple facets of the game reaffirm his status as one of baseball’s most compelling figures. The next chapter of his career will not only shape the Angels’ fortunes but also set a precedent for how the sport navigates the challenges and opportunities presented by two‑way superstars.
